# Code map

Where a feature's changes usually go, so a session can find them without surveying the repo. Find the function with `grep -n`, then read only that range with `sed -n 'A,Bp'`. Don't read big files whole (`contracts/src/index.ts` ~1,160 lines, `db/src/schema.ts` ~980, dashboard pages up to ~860).

## Layers, in the order tasks usually touch them

Each layer has its own section below, so read only the ones a task touches: `grep -n '^### ' docs/build/code-map.md`, then `sed -n` that section.

| Layer | Where |
|---|---|
| Schema | `packages/db/src/schema.ts` (Drizzle tables), `packages/db/drizzle/NNNN_*.sql` |
| Contracts | `packages/contracts/src/index.ts` |
| Gateway | `packages/llm-gateway/src/{types,registry,router,policy}.ts`, `providers/fake.ts` |
| Domain | `packages/<module>/src/*.ts`, exported from `src/index.ts` |
| Workers | `apps/<role>/src/main.ts` |
| API | `apps/api/src/<area>.ts` with `register<Area>Routes(app, deps, sessionFrom)`, wired at the end of `app.ts` |
| Dashboard | `apps/dashboard/src/router.tsx`, `pages/*.tsx`, `shell/` (nav, app shell), `lib/*.ts` |
| Widget | `apps/widget/src/loader.ts`, `panel.tsx`, `build.mjs` |
| Evals | `evals/cases/feat-NNN-<topic>.json`, `evals/thresholds.json` |

### Schema

- Latest migrations: `0043`, FEAT-043's takeover: `conversation_owners`, `messages.author_user_id`/`author_name`, the dashboard's restrictive insert policy on `messages`; `0042` is FEAT-042's inbox lifecycle: status check, `version`, close columns, `messages.task_kinds`, `inbox_queue_auto_close()` owned by `kaki_inbox_timer`.
- FEAT-046 adds `0047_message_search.sql` (`pg_trgm`, `btree_gin`, `messages_search_trgm_idx` on `(tenant_id, body gin_trgm_ops)`: substring search on message text, read through SECURITY DEFINER `inbox_search_hits(patterns)` owned by NOLOGIN `kaki_inbox_search`). Lesson: under RLS a non-leakproof operator (`ILIKE`, `~`, `@@` on text) is never an index condition; a search that must use an index goes through such a function.
- FEAT-055 adds `0049_approvals.sql`: `approvals` (`approvals_one_pending_uq`; visitor inserts, dashboard updates decision columns only), `boundary_rules.approval_sla_minutes`, `approval_candidates()`, the timer sweep `approvals_queue_due()` (owned by `kaki_approvals_timer`; it marks `expired` itself), auto-close skipping `waiting_approval`, and the notice, alert, escalation-source and card checks widened.
- FEAT-049 adds `0048_leads.sql`: `contacts`, `consents` (append-only), `leads` (`leads_one_open_uq`: one open lead per contact), `lead_settings`; `conversations.contact_id`, `messages.card`; `visitor_privacy()` also returns the marketing wording, lead fields and industry; `inbox_contact_hits()` (the 0047 pattern) for contact search.
- FEAT-045 adds `0046_suggestions.sql` (`suggestions`, dashboard zone only; `corrections_reply_edit_uq`).
- FEAT-044 adds `0045_escalations.sql` (`escalations`, `escalation_routing`, `escalation_candidates()` for member IDs from the visitor zone, `inbox_queue_escalation_reminders()`).
- `pnpm db:generate`, then add RLS, grants and checks by hand in the same or the next migration.
- New tenant table: forced RLS + policy, name in `TENANT_SCOPED_TABLES` (end of schema.ts), a case in `packages/db/test/rls.int.test.ts`.
- Views such as `visitor_facts` are in the SQL migrations.

### Contracts

Zod shapes in sections headed `// ---- Dashboard API: <area> (<FR>; FEAT-NNN §3)`. Add a new section at the end.

### Gateway

A new logical model goes in `LogicalModel` and both registries, and the fake provider must route it.

- Thin wiring and config; every variable in the role's `.env.example`.
- Cross-tenant scheduler jobs call a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by a NOLOGIN role (`cost_governor_evaluate` 0009, `kb_stale_scan` 0029, `kb_gap_cluster` 0030 from FEAT-019, `inbox_queue_auto_close` 0042 from FEAT-042: scheduler `auto-close.ts` queues an `AutoCloseJob` the agent-worker runs through `autoCloseIdle` and publishes).
- Alert email: the scheduler's `NOTIFY_SWEEP_MS` tick (FEAT-052).

- Session and role come from `sessionFrom`; tenant ID never from the body. `sessionFrom` refuses sessions still owing two-step verification (FEAT-006).
- **Sensitive actions** (AUTH-03 list) call `requireReauth(s)` from `@kaki/identity` after the capability check: 403 `reauth_required` with `methods` (contract `ReauthRequired`; test it with `staleReauth` as in `apps/api/test/mfa.int.test.ts`).
- FEAT-042: `inbox.ts` `registerInboxRoutes` (list views with keyset cursor, thread, older pages, close with `{ version }` → 409 `state_changed`/`already_closed`; publishes on `channels.inbox`).
- FEAT-043 adds there the takeover routes (`/takeover`, `/handback`, `POST /messages`, `/handover-request`, `GET /api/v1/inbox/members`), `namesIn(t)` (owner names via `memberNames`, passed to the inbox views) and `notifyMember` (`MemberEvent`s on `channels.member`, which `/ws` forwards to that member).
- Routes a pending session may use take `authFrom(req, { allow: [...] })`: `registerMfaRoutes(app, deps, { authFrom, sessionFrom })` in `mfa.ts`.
- FEAT-007: `team.ts` (`registerTeamRoutes`, the same shape) holds team, invitation and workspace routes; its error codes are `INVITATION_ERRORS`/`TEAM_ERRORS` there.
- FEAT-008: `apps/api/src/account.ts` (`registerAccountRoutes`: `/me/account`, `/me/profile`, `/me/email-change`, `/me/sessions`, public `/email-change/confirm`; all `authFrom`, so they work without a workspace).

### Evals

Agent-touching features add their own cases (plan §3).

## Agent pipeline (read this instead of `turn.ts`, `dispatch.ts`, `coach.ts`)

All in `packages/agent/src`; read a function by range only when a task changes it.

- **Visitor turn**, `runVisitorTurn` (`turn.ts`, run by agent-worker per visitor message): (1) one transaction loads the message, skips if not a visitor's or already answered, loads the boundary rules in force (approvals `rulesInForce`, FEAT-054; `DispatchContext.boundaryRules()`, `rulesVersion` in `agent.decision`), checks `aiAllowed` (`gate.ts`: kill switch, no human owner (status, and from FEAT-043 the `conversation_owners` row via inbox `ownerOf`), channel live from FEAT-034 via channels `visitorChannel`), the history, disclosure state and opening hours (after-hours notice due?). (2) Gate closed: `paused` stores the fallback text once (not repeated while the last reply is it, FEAT-057); `not_live` (FEAT-034) stores the channel's offline message once, with no model call; a human owner or closed chat stores nothing. (3) `triage` (`plan.ts`, model `triage`) runs in parallel with retrieval (`llm.embed` → kb `searchVisitorFacts` over `visitor_facts`, audited `tool.lookup_kb`). Triage gets the blocked topics as a tail on its request (none saved: no tail). Then `applyBoundary` (`boundary.ts`, FEAT-054): a blocked topic, by phrase match or triage's `blocked` topic, turns the `answer` tasks into one `out_of_scope` `blocked` task (`blocked_topic` text, no reply-model call; `guardrail.boundary_topic`). Triage never rejects (`FALLBACK_PLAN`); no facts or no plan → `unavailable` with the fallback. (4) Language from the plan, system slots (hours). (5) `dispatchPlan(visitorRegistry, plan, ctx)` runs the non-answer tasks; a safety `endTurn` stores the safety text and ends. (6) `routeReply` picks `reply.simple`/`reply.complex` (ADR-007), then `answerTurn` (`answer.ts`: fixed AGT-04 texts or `composeReply`). (7) `store()` appends the reply, disclosure and notice, and audits guardrail hits plus one `agent.decision` (codes and IDs only, ADR-014); from FEAT-019 it also marks the visitor message as a coverage gap (`markQuestionGap`, inbox) when an `answer` turn ends `unavailable`, `unsure` or `escalated`.
- **Compose**, `composeReply` (`compose.ts`): the model writes text with slot markers (`prompt.ts`); each segment goes `renderSegment` (`render.ts`, fills prices, dates, policies from facts, ADR-008) → `verifySegment` (`verify.ts`; its `policy` kind already blocks model-typed "refund", "guarantee", "money back", "deliver by", 保证 and 退款, so test phrasings that avoid those words) → leak guard (`guard.ts`; `ruleText` cuts `system` at the `<business>` line, so anything the prompt puts after it is tenant data, not rules) → boundary guard (`boundary.ts` `boundaryGuard`: discount offers, forbidden commitments and custom phrases from the rules block in the prompt's cached tenant part, FEAT-054) → released (streamed via `publishSegment`) only if all pass and the gate is still open. A failure regenerates once on `reply.complex` with the released prefix, then escalates. Provider failure keeps what was released and closes with the fallback.
- **Dispatcher** (`dispatch.ts`, ADR-025): `TaskKind`s are in `plan.ts`. A `TaskHandler` declares `kind`, `scopes` (`visitor`/`coaching`), a Zod `args`, optional `needsConsent`/`checkBoundary`, and `run(ctx, args, idempotencyKey)`. `check()` in order: scope → gate open → args parse → consent → boundary, else `refused` with that reason. `dispatchPlan` runs safety tasks (`crisis`, `abuse`) before state tasks, each in plan order; every task is audited `agent.dispatch`; a thrown handler is `failed` without dropping the rest; no handler is `unhandled`. State tasks may return a `reply` key (`out_of_scope`, `advice`, …) for the composer. `dispatchToolCall` treats a model tool call as a proposal: refused unless its kind is in the plan and scope. FEAT-044 registers `escalateHandler` (`ConversationPort.escalate`); the widget's Talk to a person button skips the model and calls inbox `requestEscalation` directly. Registries: `visitorRegistry` (`dispatch.ts`), `coachingRegistry` (`coach-dispatch.ts`, `proposeCorrectionHandler`). New features add a handler to a registry, never a new path.
- **Lead capture** (FEAT-049; `lead.ts`, handler in `dispatch.ts` to avoid a cycle): `captureLeadHandler` (`needsConsent`) returns a `lead_form` card and writes nothing; the dispatcher's `consent` refusal makes the turn attach a `consent` card; `store()` adds one consent offer per conversation to unavailable, unsure, out-of-scope, after-hours and fallback replies (never safety turns, never after a decline or capture): the rule is `cardForReply`/`consentCardFor` in `lead.ts`, shared with the eval runner. `consentGiven()` reads leads `consentState` for the conversation. The lead itself is written only by the widget's form submit (`/widget/v1/conversations/:id/lead`).
- **Approvals** (FEAT-055, planned; `approval.ts`): `requestCommitmentHandler` (tool `draft_approval`) calls `ConversationPort.draftApproval`, which runs approvals `draftApproval` with this turn's retrieved facts; a commitment-only turn stores the waiting notice (`approvalNotice`) with no reply model, like an escalate-only turn. The quote reaches the visitor only through approvals `deliver` after a decision, never the composer.
- **Coaching turn**, `runCoachingTurn` (`coach.ts`, called by the API, FEAT-027): masks PII, loads the session (`coach-store.ts`), plans; a `correct` task goes to `proposeChange` (`propose.ts`) → a kb correction proposal, never a fact edit (ADR-010); otherwise it answers as a visitor would plus `explain()` (which facts, why, `VisitorsWouldGet`). `reanswer` re-asks the original question once a correction is applied, giving before and after.
- **Suggested reply**, `suggestReply` (`suggest.ts`, FEAT-045, called by the API synchronously like replay): owner/pause/rate checks, the latest visitor message, triage + approved-only `searchCoachingFacts`, `replayRegistry` (no side effects), `answerStep` (shared with coach and replay; takes `meta` from the caller) → a `suggestions` row, never a message. Sending with `suggestionId`: inbox `recordSuggestionUse`, and kb `proposeReplyEdit` (`reply_edit` correction) when edited.
- **Reply prompt layout** (`prompt.ts` `buildVisitorPrompt`): fixed platform rules, then the cached tenant block (`<business>`, `assistantLines`, `rulesLines`' `<rules>`), then per-turn facts and slots; triage's per-tenant data goes in the uncached `tail` after the fixed `TRIAGE_SYSTEM` (`plan.ts`).
- **Per-tenant turn state** (rules, profile, assistant settings) loads in one transaction per flow: visitor in `runVisitorTurn`'s first transaction, coaching in `prepare(` (`coach.ts`, dashboard zone), replay in `prepareQuestion(` (`replay.ts`). A feature that adds turn state adds it in all three.
- **Fakes** for tests and evals: `fake-triage.ts`, `fake-responder.ts`, `fake-coach.ts`; the gateway's `providers/fake.ts` routes every logical model.

## Tests

- Unit: `src/**/*.test.ts` next to the code. `pnpm --filter <pkg> test`.
- Integration: `<pkg>/test/*.int.test.ts`, real Postgres via `startTestDatabase()` and `TENANT_A`/`TENANT_B` from `@kaki/db/testing`. API helpers in `apps/api/test/support.ts` (`testApp(tdb, …)`, `sessionCookie(tdb, email)`, `fakeMailer`, `testConfig`). Write a new suite from these names; read a neighbour's setup and one case only. Without Docker: `scripts/test-env.sh pnpm --filter <pkg> test:integration`.
- Cross-tenant: every new route or table gets a tenant-B-can't-see-tenant-A case.
- Dev seed: `packages/db/src/setup.ts` (`devTenants`, `seed`): fixed tenant IDs, profiles, the widget seeded live, terms at `SEED_TERMS_VERSION`. A feature whose new state the dev tenants need (e.g. FEAT-035's onboarding row) adds it in `seed`.
- E2E: `e2e/tests/<area>.e2e.ts`, helpers in `e2e/tests/support.ts` (`signIn`, `expectNoSeriousA11yViolations`, `openShadowRoots`). Runs in CI.
- E2E pitfalls (each cost a local CI run in FEAT-032; details in its `handoff.md`):
  - A cross-origin response without a CORS header is `requestfailed` in Chromium and WebKit, never `response`, so `waitForResponse` hangs. Read it through `page.route` + `route.fetch()` (keeps the Origin): `configAnswer` in `widget-install.e2e.ts`.
  - WebKit's trace adds `__playwright_*` globals to the page; filter them out of "no globals added" checks.
  - JSX like `{busy && <span/>} {caption}` puts a leading space in the text, so `getByText(/^…/)` misses it. Use the role (`getByRole('status')`) with `toHaveText` and an unanchored pattern, and wait for the in-progress text first so an earlier result can't pass.
  - An axe check at phone width runs at a tall viewport (`{ width: 375, height: 5000 }`): the fixed tab bar otherwise covers whatever targets sit at the bottom and WebKit reports `target-size` (FEAT-054; `conflicts.e2e.ts`).
  - A step that waits on a worker (detection, crawl, extraction) needs `test.setTimeout` above the default 60 s, as the ingest specs have.
  - A spec that changes shared dev-tenant state part-way (an allowed origin) restores it in `afterEach` on failure; otherwise the next browser's run fails and leaves data that breaks later specs. After a failed run: `pnpm stack:reset`, `pnpm db:setup`.
  - Before asking Ken for CI, run the spec's tricky steps in the cloud session's Chromium against the widget dev server with a stubbed config.

## Design docs, read by section

- Plan row: `grep -n 'FEAT-NNN' docs/03-planning/implementation-plan.md`.
- FR / UC / NFR: `grep -n '<ID>' docs/01-requirements/SRS.md` (and `use-cases.md`), then `sed -n` the block.
- Screens: `grep -n 'SCR-APP-NNN' docs/02-design/ux-foundations.md docs/design-manifest.json`.
- ADRs: `docs/02-design/adr/ADR-NNN-*.md`; the invariants in `AGENTS.md` usually suffice.
- Format to copy: the newest feature folder (`ls docs/features`). Read its headings (`grep -n '^## '`), not the whole file. The pattern is below.

## Feature document pattern

- `technical-design.md`: 1 Intent · 2 Codebase context · 3 API contracts · 4 Schema changes · 5 Component design · 6 Acceptance criteria (AC-n, each traced to an FR criterion or UC step) · 7 Decisions (D-n) · 8 Escalations and open items · 9 Self-check. About 200–250 lines.
- `tasks.md`: header `> Executes: …` and `> Status: designed | developer-done | accepted · Last updated`. Tasks `- [ ] Tn — <what> (design §, AC-n)` with an indented `Done when:` line, and `Note:` lines for anything left to CI. The last task is Verify and ends with a "Verification evidence" section, one bullet per AC.
- `ui-design.md`: one section per SCR ID with states (empty, loading, error with a next action), copy, and token use; plus entries in `docs/design-manifest.json`.
- `acceptance-report.md`: verdict line, standard, repo state audited, verdict summary, then per-AC evidence, the test-diff review and the invariant review.

## Big files by anchor

Jump with `grep -n '<anchor>' <file>`, then `sed -n` ~40–80 lines from there. List a file's functions with `grep -n '^export \|^async function\|^function' <file>`. Anchors, not line numbers, so they survive edits.

- `packages/inbox/src/index.ts` (~760, conversations and messages; FEAT-042 adds `lifecycle.ts`, the only writer of `conversations.status`, `views.ts` (list, counts, thread, events, sidebar) and `mappers.ts` (`toMessage`/`toSummary`); kb `chips.ts` `factChips`, identity `names.ts` `memberNames`): `appendVisitorMessage(` (reopen, FEAT-042), `appendAgentReply(`, `listConversations(`, `flagConversation(`, `endAiConversation(`, `endVisitorConversation(`. Audit entries are read back for the thread's state dividers (`threadEvents`). FEAT-043: `ownership.ts` (`takeOver`, `handBack`, `requestHandover`, `sendStaffMessage`, `staffNotice`, `ownerOf`/`ownersOf`); `transition` deletes the owner row on every close and on `human → ai`; `listConversations`/`conversationSummary` take an `OwnerNames` resolver for `ConversationSummary.owner`; `toThreadEvent` maps audit rows to dividers. FEAT-046: `search.ts` (`searchConversations`, `searchPatterns`, `excerptOf`; POST `/api/v1/conversations/search`, the text never in a URL). FEAT-044: `escalation.ts` (`requestEscalation`, `route`, `remindEscalation`, `escalationsOf`); `transition` resolves the open escalation and cancels its alerts on every move out of `escalated`. `apps/agent-worker/src/main.ts` `TurnJob` (turns, and from FEAT-042 the auto-close job).
- `packages/agent/src/turn.ts` (~370 lines, one big `runVisitorTurn`): `async function store(` (stores the reply, audits the decision; turn outcomes are recorded here), `searchVisitorFacts(` (the retrieval step), `aiAllowed(` (the gate check), `dispatchPlan(`, `answerTurn(`.
- `packages/agent/src/coach.ts` (~700): `async function prepare(` (tenant state), `export async function answerStep(`, `runCoachingTurn(`, `reanswer(`. `replay.ts` (~480): `prepareQuestion(` (tenant state), `replayQuestion(`, `replayNext(`.
- `apps/api/src/corrections.ts` (~340): helpers `toItem`, `itemOf`, `contextOf`, `kbEditOf`, `toReplay` above `registerCorrectionRoutes`; inside it, find a route by its path (`grep -n "app\.\(get\|post\)" <file>`). Other `apps/api/src/<area>.ts` files follow the same shape.
- `apps/api/src/app.ts` (~700): the widget routes sit together from `app.post('/widget/v1/conversations'` to `'/widget/v1/conversations/:id/escalate'` (`visitorFrom`, the visitor-owns-conversation check, `notify`); `governance/src/privacy.ts`: `DEFAULT_PURPOSE`, `CONSENT_PROMPT`, `visitorPrivacy(` near the end.
- `apps/dashboard/src/pages/privacy-parts.tsx` (~670, the settings-form pattern): read `function useSave(` (save → toast → error mapping) and `export function ErrorSummary(` and one form (`export function PurposeForm(`), not the whole file. `rules-parts.tsx` (FEAT-054) follows it.
- `apps/dashboard/src/pages/correction.tsx` (~780): `CorrectionPage` (main body, most of the file), `Origin`, `FixDiff`, `PastAnswers`, `EditFixDialog`, `EditFixForm`. Other big pages split into named function components the same way.
- Sign-in internals (FEAT-007 design read these by range): `packages/identity/src/users.ts` `startSession(` (which tenant a new session opens), `magic-link.ts` `consumeMagicLink(` (the atomic claim, then sign-in or re-auth), `sessions.ts` `authenticate(` (one query: session, user, membership, MFA state); `apps/api/src/auth.ts` `authFrom(`/`sessionFrom(` near the top, routes below; `apps/realtime/src/app.ts` `app.get('/ws'` (authenticates once at connect, then subscribes).
